_meta.rule: A correlation is published only when every variable it correlates is an official league fact or a function of one. Anything that needs a market price, a model output or a third-party figure is left blank with a reason. n is on every row.
_meta.interval: Two-sided 95% Fisher-z interval on the published r or phi.
_meta.official_figures_used: Final scores only: home_score and away_score, 1999-2026 regular season, transcribed into the pinned dataset and, for 2026, reconciled club by club against the league's own standings page.

table_a_official.pair: Home margin vs game total (same game)
table_a_official.note: Both are arithmetic on the official final score. A positive value means the home team tends to win by more in high-scoring games.

table_a_official.pair: Home points vs away points (same game)
table_a_official.note: The two halves of one official scoreline. This is the number a same-game totals parlay actually rests on.

table_a_official.pair: Team points scored, consecutive games (same team, t vs t+1)
table_a_official.note: Autocorrelation of an official scoreboard quantity. If this were strongly positive it would be a scoreboard fact worth trading on; the interval is what decides that.

table_a_official.pair: Team points conceded, consecutive games (same team, t vs t+1)
table_a_official.note: Autocorrelation of an official scoreboard quantity. If this were strongly positive it would be a scoreboard fact worth trading on; the interval is what decides that.

table_a_official.pair: Team margin, consecutive games (same team, t vs t+1)
table_a_official.note: Autocorrelation of an official scoreboard quantity. If this were strongly positive it would be a scoreboard fact worth trading on; the interval is what decides that.

table_a_official.pair: League mean game total, consecutive weeks (t vs t+1)
table_a_official.note: Whether a high-scoring week is followed by another. One point per week; n is the number of consecutive week pairs.

table_a_official.pair: Team-season points for vs points against
table_a_official.note: One point per team-season, seasons 1999-2025 only. 2026 is excluded because the season is in progress and its totals are not final.

table_a_official.pair: Team-season scoring rate, season t vs t+1
table_a_official.note: How much of a club's scoring rate survives into the next season. One point per consecutive team-season pair.

table_b_parlay_legs.pair: Same-game card: our side leg vs our total leg
table_b_parlay_legs.note: Both legs are defined against the line this repository originates, so each leg's outcome is a function of the official final score alone. The dependence measured here is therefore officially sourced. A negative phi means the legs win together less often than independence implies, so a card priced at the product of the two legs is worse for the bettor than its price suggests.

table_b_parlay_legs.pair: Cross-game card: the week's two largest side legs
table_b_parlay_legs.note: Two games, so there is no shared-score reason for dependence; the measurement is the test of whether one exists. A negative phi means the legs win together less often than independence implies, so a card priced at the product of the two legs is worse for the bettor than its price suggests.

table_c_not_computable.pair: Market spread cover vs market total over (same game)
table_c_not_computable.why: Both legs are defined by a market number. No official publisher prints NFL spreads or totals, so there is no officially sourced input to correlate.
table_c_not_computable.unblock: Admit the pinned third-party market file as an input, or originate the legs against our own numbers (which is what Table B does).

table_c_not_computable.pair: Our fair-vs-market difference vs the settled outcome
table_c_not_computable.why: One side of the pair is a market price. Our own fair number is reproducible, the market's is not officially published.
table_c_not_computable.unblock: Same choice. Until it is made, the leaderboard reports ROI at the recorded close and flags the convention.

table_c_not_computable.pair: Correlation a two-leg card needs to break even
table_c_not_computable.why: The threshold is arithmetic on the two leg prices. Prices are not officially published, so the threshold cannot be stated as an officially sourced number.
table_c_not_computable.unblock: Decide the price-input question. The formula is published on the page; only the input is missing.

table_c_not_computable.why: No official publisher prints player-prop prices, and no official player-level log is reachable from this repository. There is nothing to correlate.
table_c_not_computable.unblock: Acquire an official or licensed player feed. The schema is committed and every value is blank until then.

ties.note: A regular-season game can end tied. This is the base rate a moneyline settlement rule has to handle; it is published because the fair-price column depends on it.
